english.note: Use this as the all-purpose spoken choice when something is achieved or perceived only with difficulty or by a narrow margin.
Use this when marginally means barely sufficiently or only just managing to do something, rather than simply slightly.
Use this when someone only just succeeds, such as narrowly winning or barely avoiding something.
Use this for “barely” or “only just,” when someone manages something with little margin.

examples.english: I barely managed to catch the train.
examples.traditional: 我勉強先至趕得切班車。

english.note: Use 勉強 as the concise all-purpose choice when someone does something despite not wanting to.

examples.english: I reluctantly agreed to help him move.
examples.traditional: 我勉強應承咗幫佢搬屋。
